_comment: Tier-2 for dune::stokes (preconditioner names are a five-item enumeration). The catalog advertised PETSc fieldsplit, AMG and ILU as preconditioners for this backend; for the default numpy/'fem' storage none of those names exists. dune-fem forwards 'linear.preconditioning.method' unchecked to DUNE's parameter reader, so a plausible name fails at SCHEME CONSTRUCTION with a RuntimeError naming 'fem.solver.linear.preconditioning.method' and enumerating none, sor, ssor, gauss-seidel, jacobi. That exact message was captured live twice on 2026-08-03 from two independent scripts (a Taylor-Hood Stokes script passing 'ilu', and a Poisson script passing a nonsense name), which is the evidence behind expect_in_output below. PROVENANCE CAVEAT: this fixture SCRIPT has not itself been observed to run green end to end — the machine was saturated by unrelated jobs during the writing pass and the single JIT scheme build did not finish inside the timeout. The parts that were not directly observed (that each of the five advertised names really builds and solves) are therefore asserted by the script's own fail-fast logic, which prints a FAIL: line and returns 1, rather than by expect_in_output. Promote them into expect_in_output once the fixture has been seen green on a quiet machine. MUTATION CONTROL (2026-08-07): T2_MUTATE=1 puts three names the enumeration DOES accept -- jacobi, sor, ssor -- in the slot where the base run puts ilu, amg and fieldsplit, i.e. the pathology removed. Measured 2026-08-07 on dune-fem 2.12.0.2: unmutated the first half prints bogus_ilu_rejected=True, bogus_amg_rejected=True and bogus_fieldsplit_rejected=True; mutated it prints bogus_jacobi_rejected=False, bogus_sor_rejected=False and bogus_ssor_rejected=False, so all three expectations stop being printed and three `FAIL: preconditioner '<name>' was accepted` lines appear -- and the forbidden token FAIL: with them. The verdict is settled inside the first minute, before the expensive half. Re-verify with `cd <fixture dir> && T2_MUTATE=1 ~/miniconda3/envs/dune-fem-env/bin/python source.py`. RUNTIME CAVEAT, measured twice on 2026-08-07: this fixture does NOT run to completion on this host. Its second half solves the same 4x4 Poisson problem once per advertised preconditioner at linear.tolerance 1e-12 with no maxiterations cap; run under exactly the runner's own limit, `timeout 2400 python source.py` exited 124 having printed only as far as pc_none_converged=True -- i.e. it was still inside the `sor` solve after 40 minutes. An untimed run reached pc_sor_converged=False and was still inside `gauss-seidel` when it was stopped at 60 minutes. So scripts/run_tier2_fixtures.py records this fixture as failed-by-timeout on this machine, not as passed. That is why the unmutated half of the control above is quoted from the fixture's own first-half output rather than from a completed run. SEPARATE FINDING (2026-08-07): the docstring says this fixture 'proves each advertised name really does build and solve', and it prints pc_<name>_converged for all five -- but a converged=False is NOT added to the fail list; only a raised exception is, and no pc_<name>_converged string is in expect_in_output. pc_sor_converged=False was observed in both runs and changed nothing. So the second half of this fixture's stated claim is printed but not enforced. ENVIRONMENT: there is no ofa-dune conda env on this host, which is the interpreter scripts/run_tier2_fixtures.py falls back to; dune-fem 2.12.0.2 lives in ~/miniconda3/envs/dune-fem-env. Without DUNE_PYTHON set to that interpreter the runner records this fixture as `skipped`, not `failed`, so a summary that counts only passes and failures shows nothing wrong while nothing was executed.
